explore.heading: How the system is built

items.title: How the system works
items.detail: The system is built as a layered token architecture. Core values form the foundation, brand tokens define identity, semantic layers translate those values into UI decisions, and component tokens keep the interface consistent.

items.title: One system. Multiple brands.
items.detail: A shared product foundation supports multiple visual identities. Brand and theme tokens can re-skin the interface without rebuilding its components or product logic.

items.title: Built for production
items.detail: The system connects design and implementation through reusable components, design tokens and automated checks — helping keep Figma and production UI aligned as the product scales.

caseAurum.title: Aurum Multibrand
caseAurum.lead: One casino lobby in four brands, light and dark, on one set of components. A working model of the system I build for teams that run more than one brand.
caseAurum.context: White-label and iGaming platforms ship one product under several brands. Each brand wants its own colors, type and shapes; the product team wants one codebase. Aurum Multibrand models that setup: a casino lobby with promos, game tiles, tournaments, a shop and account screens, styled only by tokens. Switch the brand or the theme and the whole interface re-skins without a reload.

problems.title: Brand values live in components
problems.detail: When colors and radii sit inside a button or a card, every new brand means editing every component.

problems.title: Brands multiply with themes
problems.detail: Four brands in light and dark are eight combinations. Kept by hand, they drift out of sync.

problems.title: Design and code drift apart
problems.detail: Variables in Figma and CSS in the repository are edited separately, and contrast is checked by eye.

caseAurum.solutionLead: Six token layers. Components ask for a meaning, the theme maps meanings to the brand, and only the brand file holds raw values. Tokens Studio pushes JSON to GitHub, a build script turns it into CSS variables and checks it.

layers.components: What each component asks for: button.primary.bg, chip.selected.bg.
layers.theme: Meanings for light and dark: fill, text, border, surface.
layers.typography: Text styles shared by every brand.
layers.map: Ramps generated from brand colors: 100 to 900.
layers.brand: The only per-brand file: colors, fonts, radii, spacing.

shotsCaption: The Brand collection in Figma: one mode per brand, same variable names.
The commit that added Ultra: a new brand file and theme entries. components.json is not touched.

results.label: values in a brand file
results.detail: The same keys in every brand. A new brand is a copy of this file with new values.

results.label: changes in components for a new brand
results.detail: Components reference meanings only. The checker fails the build if one reaches for a raw value.

results.label: brand × theme combinations
results.detail: From one component library and one CSS file, switched by two attributes on the root element.

caseAurum.different: I would add automated contrast checks before the second brand, not after the fourth. When the checker arrived, it found that text.accent in the light theme misses WCAG AA in every brand: Aurum 2.13, Nova 1.67, Fiesta 1.42, Ultra 3.03 against the required 4.5. The good news is where the fix lives: one change in the shared theme layer corrects all four brands at once.
